body.en: append(x) adds x as one element at the end. extend(list2) adds each element of list2. insert(i, x) puts x at index i. remove(x) deletes the first occurrence of value x. pop(i) removes and returns the element at index i, or the last element if no index is given. clear() empties the list.
body.kn: append(x) ಕೊನೆಗೆ ಒಂದು ಅಂಶ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. extend() ಮತ್ತೊಂದು ಲಿಸ್ಟ್‌ನ ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಂಶ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. insert(i, x) ಇಂಡೆಕ್ಸ್ i ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. remove(x) ಮೊದಲ x ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. pop(i) ತೆಗೆದು ಹಿಂದಿರುಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

heading.en: List Methods, Copying, Nested Lists and Functions

tagline.en: append, extend, insert, count, index, remove, pop, reverse, sort, sorted, min, max, sum; aliasing versus copying; nested lists; and lists passed to functions.

myth.en: L = L.sort() sorts L and keeps the sorted list.

truth.en: L.sort() sorts in place and returns None, so L = L.sort() makes L None. Write L.sort() alone, or L = sorted(L). Most string methods return a new string, so learners expect list methods to do the same. List methods that change the list (append, sort, reverse…) return None.

say.en: append adds one element; extend adds each element of a sequence.
remove works by value, pop by index (and returns the element).
sort() changes the list and returns None; sorted() returns a new list.
b = a is an alias; a.copy(), a[:], list(a) make copies.
A function that changes a passed list's elements changes the caller's list.

goal.en: append, extend, insert, count, index, remove, pop, reverse, sort, sorted, min, max, sum; aliasing versus copying; nested lists; and lists passed to functions.

question.en: L = [1, 2]. After L.append([3, 4]), what is len(L)?

explain.en: append adds its argument as one element: [1, 2, [3, 4]]. extend would give [1, 2, 3, 4], length 4.

task.en: a = [1, 2]; b = a; b[0] = 9. What is a?

question.en: a = [1, 2]; b = a; b[0] = 9. What is a?

explain.en: b = a makes an alias, not a copy. Both names point to one list, so changing b[0] changes what a shows. Use a.copy() for a separate list.

takeaway.en: append adds one element; extend adds each element of a sequence.

narration.en: Many people think: L = L.sort() sorts L and keeps the sorted list. Actually: L.sort() sorts in place and returns None, so L = L.sort() makes L None. Write L.sort() alone, or L = sorted(L). Most string methods return a new string, so learners expect list methods to do the same. List methods that change the list (append, sort, reverse…) return None.
